is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles coluzzii.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports on genetic variation (missense variants) within the Cyp6m2 gene, which is not among the required insecticide-resistance markers listed in the instructions.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 provides population allele frequencies for 15 non-synonymous variants in the Cyp6m2 gene across 16 populations.

african_field_population.evidence: The study uses Ag1000G Phase 2 data, which consists of wild-caught mosquitoes from 13 African countries.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study analyzing genomic data from the Ag1000G project.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study uses data from 33 sampling sites across 16 populations in 13 countries (Table 1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The mosquitoes were collected between 2000 and 2012, which is a defined collection period.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper explicitly states it uses data from the Ag1000G Phase 2 data resource (e.g., page 5, 'Short-read whole-genome sequence data from the Ag1000G phase 2 data resource [47] were used...').

supplement.evidence: The necessary data (allele frequencies) is provided in Table 1 of the main text.

assessment.summary: This study analyzes genetic variation in the Cyp6m2 gene using whole-genome sequence data from 1142 wild-caught Anopheles gambiae and An. coluzzii mosquitoes from 13 African countries (Ag1000G Phase 2). It identifies 15 high-frequency missense variants but finds no evidence of directional selection on these variants, suggesting that Cyp6m2-associated resistance may be driven by regulatory mechanisms rather than missense mutations.
exclusion_reasons: The paper does not report on any of the required insecticide-resistance markers (e.g., kdr, Ace-1, Rdl, GSTe2, etc.).
